summary: Snapshot evidence shows the page renders a single native submit control labeled 'Click' as <input type='submit' id='submit-id-submit'> inside a POST form. Activating it keeps the same URL, triggers a navigation lifecycle caused by form submission, and displays the visible feedback text 'Submitted'. Keyboard activation is supported by native control behavior.

acceptanceCriteria.criterion: The page loads and displays a single native submit control labeled 'Click'
The control is visible and enabled by default
Clicking the control submits the form and displays the visible confirmation text 'Submitted'
Submission keeps the user on the same page URL even though a form-submit navigation lifecycle occurs
The control is accessible via keyboard (Tab to focus, Enter and Space to activate)
The interactive element is native form markup (<input type='submit'>), not a styled link

testScenarios.scenario: Submit control is present and enabled on page load
testScenarios.expectedResult: A single visible enabled control labeled 'Click' is present

testScenarios.scenario: Clicking the submit control displays the real confirmation text
testScenarios.expectedResult: The page shows visible confirmation text exactly equal to 'Submitted'

testScenarios.scenario: Form submission keeps the same page URL
steps: Wait for the resulting page state to settle
testScenarios.expectedResult: The final URL remains https://www.qa-practice.com/elements/button/simple even though a form submit lifecycle occurs

testScenarios.scenario: Submit control is reachable and activatable by keyboard
steps: Press Tab until the 'Click' control receives focus
Repeat from a fresh page load using Space
testScenarios.expectedResult: The control receives focus and both Enter and Space result in the same visible 'Submitted' feedback

testScenarios.scenario: Interactive element is native submit markup
testScenarios.expectedResult: The element is <input type='submit' id='submit-id-submit'>, not <a>

testScenarios.scenario: Revisiting and re-submitting does not break the page
steps: Navigate back to the initial state if needed and repeat
Observe the page state after each submission
testScenarios.expectedResult: Each run ends with the same visible 'Submitted' feedback and no broken layout or error state

assumptions.assumption: The confirmation text is rendered in #result after the form post returns to the same route
No authentication or session state is required to interact with the control

risks.risk: A generator that assumes no navigation may under-model this page because same-URL form submit still triggers navigation events
risks.recommendation: Assert same final URL and visible confirmation instead of assuming zero navigation lifecycle events

risks.risk: The snapshot does not show post-submit DOM, only pre-submit page structure
risks.recommendation: Keep one runtime validation that confirms #result renders Submitted after activation

recommendation.comment: Snapshot and runtime evidence resolve the earlier ambiguity. The feature is fully automatable with exact assertions for control type and the Submitted feedback.
